"Ölstand prüfen, wenn Ölverlust festgestellt wird oder wenn Schaltstörungen auftreten. Der Ölstand sollte dann in einer Mercedes-Benz Service-Station richtiggestellt werden. 

Ölstand nur bei betriebswarmem Getriebe und waagerecht stehendem Fahrzeug prüfen. Dazu den Motor laufen lassen, das Getriebe in Stellung „P“ schalten und die Feststellbremse betätigen."

**(Translation summary:** Check oil level if loss is detected or shifting issues occur. Correct at a service station. Check only when the transmission is at operating temperature and the car is level, with the engine running in "P" and parking brake applied.)

**Right Column Text (General Procedure):**
"Verschlußhebel lösen (1) und Ölmeßstab herausziehen. Meßstab mit einem fusselfreien Tuch abwischen und zum Messen ganz einstecken. Meßstab herausziehen und Ölstand ablesen – er soll zwischen der Min- und Max-Marke liegen. 

Abschließend den Meßstab ganz einstecken und mit dem Verschlußhebel sichern (2).

**Hinweise:** 
Die Betriebstemperatur ist nach **ca. 10 km** Fahrt erreicht. 

Bei abgekühltem Getriebe wird ein geringerer Ölstand angezeigt – auf keinen Fall Öl nachfüllen. 

Die Max-Marke darf nicht überschritten werden. Eventuell zuviel eingefülltes Öl muß abgelassen oder abgesaugt werden. 

Füllmenge siehe „Betriebsstoffe“, Seite 142."

**(Translation summary:** Release lever (1), pull dipstick, wipe with lint-free cloth, re-insert fully. Read level (must be between Min/Max). Re-insert and lock (2). Notes: Operating temp reached after ~10km. Do not top up when cold. Do not exceed Max mark. Refer to page 142 for fill quantities.)

### **Additional Page Elements**
*   **Page Number:** 107 (bottom right)
*   **Vertical Margin Text (right side):** Praktische Ratschläge (Practical Tips)
*   **Color Block:** There is a solid red square/rectangle in the right margin.

### Section 1: Kofferraumleuchte (Trunk Light)
*   **Diagram (P82-0007-B13A):** Shows the interior trunk light assembly. A red arrow indicates that the switch can be pushed to the left.
*   **Components:** Kofferraumleuchte (Trunk light).
*   **Text Summary:** Explains how to manually turn off the trunk light using the car key by sliding the switch to the left. This is done to prevent battery drainage if the trunk remains open for an extended period. The light automatically resets to the "on" position once the trunk is closed and reopened.

### Section 2: Warndreieck (Warning Triangle)
*   **Diagram (P88-5015-B13):** Illustrates the warning triangle mounted on the inside of the trunk lid.
*   **Labels:**
    *   **1**: A locking latch. A curved red arrow indicates it should be rotated clockwise (to the right).
    *   **Upward arrow**: Indicates the removal direction of the triangle.
*   **Components:** Warndreieck (Warning triangle).
*   **Text Summary:** States that the warning triangle is attached to the inside of the trunk lid. To remove it, turn the latch (1) to the right and lift the triangle upwards.

### Section 3: Reserverad (Spare Wheel)
*   **Diagram (P98.2010-B13):** Shows the spare wheel well under the trunk floor.
*   **Labels:**
    *   **1**: Kofferraumboden (Trunk floor panel).
    *   **2**: Lasche (Strap/Latch) used to hold the floor panel open.
*   **Components:** Reserverad (Spare wheel), Wagenheber (Jack).
*   **Text Summary:** Instructs to fold back the floor mat, lift the trunk floor panel (1), and hook the strap (2) into the holder on the trunk lid. It specifies to remove the jack first, then the spare wheel. Installation is the reverse of removal.

This technical diagram and instruction page are from a Mercedes-Benz R129 owner's manual or service document, detailing the storage of the jack and spare wheel, and providing safety information regarding tire and wheel changes.

### **Numbered Components (from the illustration):**
*   **1: Einsteckbolzen** (Insertion bolt/jacking pin)
*   **2: Wagenheberfuß** (Jack base/foot)
*   **3: Bordwerkzeug** (On-board tool kit)

### **Diagram Details & Connections:**
*   **Storage Layout:** The diagram shows the spare tire mounted vertically in the trunk. The jack is stored in a dedicated vertical bracket next to the wheel.
*   **Positioning:** The on-board tool kit (**3**) is positioned directly underneath the jack.
*   **Mechanical Setting:** For proper storage, the insertion bolt (**1**) must be screwed back (retracted) until it is almost flush with the jack foot (**2**).
*   **Reference Code:** A small technical code, **P58-0034-813A**, is visible at the bottom of the black-and-white illustration.

### **Technical Instructions & Text:**
*   **Removal/Installation:** Always remove the jack first, then the spare wheel. Re-install in reverse order.
*   **Safety Warning (Achtung!):** The jack is only for brief lifting during a wheel change. Jack stands (Unterstellböcke) must be used if working under the vehicle.
*   **First Aid Kit (Verbandstasche):** Located in the trunk in the left-hand well/recess.
*   **Wheels and Tires (Reifen, Scheibenräder):** 
    *   Only use approved tire and wheel combinations to ensure proper clearance from the brake system.
    *   The use of spacers (Distanzscheiben) is not permitted.
    *   Summer tires should only be mounted on light-alloy (Leichtmetall) wheels.
    *   Dimensions and specifications are referred to the "Technical Data" section.

### **Other Information:**
*   **Page Number:** 109
*   **Section Header:** Praktische Ratschläge (Practical Advice)
*   **Wire Colors:** None present.
*   **Part Numbers:** No individual part numbers are listed, only the diagram reference code.

[Image: r129_betriebsanleitung_1991_1993_de_p113_img1.jpeg]
This image is a technical page (page 111) from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service document titled "Praktische Ratschläge" (Practical Advice). It details tire maintenance, the CTS run-flat tire system, and different types of wheel bolts.

### Component Names and Descriptions
The diagram in the upper right illustrates four specific items related to wheel mounting:
*   **1: Wheel Bolt for Light-Alloy Wheels (Nur für Leichtmetallrad):** A longer bolt with a spherical seat design.
*   **2: Wheel Bolt for Steel Wheels (Nur für Stahlblechrad):** A shorter bolt specifically for sheet steel wheels.
*   **3: Anti-Theft Wheel Bolt (Radschraube mit Diebstahlsicherung):** A locking wheel bolt intended for light-alloy wheels.
*   **4: Wrench Adapter (Zwischenstück für Radschlüssel):** The specialized key/adapter used with the anti-theft bolt.

### Connections
*   The **Wrench Adapter (4)** is designed to interlock with the patterned head of the **Anti-Theft Wheel Bolt (3)** to allow for installation or removal using a standard wheel wrench.
*   The bolts (1, 2, 3) are used to secure either light-alloy or sheet steel wheels to the vehicle's wheel hub.

### Measurements and Limits
The text specifies critical operational limits for "CTS-Bereifung" (run-flat tires) when driving with a loss of air pressure:
*   **Maximum Speed:** Do not exceed **80 km/h**.
*   **Maximum Distance:** A maximum of **200 km** can be driven if immediate replacement is not possible.

### Part and Reference Numbers
*   **Diagram Reference Number:** P40-0016-213 (located in the bottom right corner of the illustration box).
*   **Page Number:** 111.

### Wire Colors
*   **N/A:** This is a mechanical diagram; there are no electrical wires or colors shown.

### Visible Text
**Headings:**
*   **CTS-Bereifung:** (CTS Tires)
*   **Praktische Ratschläge:** (Practical Advice - located vertically on the right red banner)

**Main Text (Summary):**
*   **Wheel Maintenance:** Rim flanges of light-alloy wheels must be checked for wear/burrs. Rusted steel wheels must be cleaned and repainted. Only drive steel wheels with wheel covers installed to prevent valve damage.
*   **CTS Tires:** Describes the run-flat properties that prevent the tire from coming off the rim. Emphasizes that driving behavior changes when tires are depressurized and that wheels/tires must be inspected by a Mercedes-Benz Service Station after run-flat use.
*   **Radschrauben beachten! (Observe wheel bolts!):** Legend for items 1 through 4 as listed in the Component Names section.

[Image: r129_betriebsanleitung_1991_1993_de_p114_img1.jpeg]
This image is page 112 from a German Mercedes-Benz R129 owner's manual or service document, titled **"Radwechsel"** (Wheel change). It provides instructions and safety warnings for changing a tire.

### **Header and Warnings**
*   **Radwechsel**: Title in red.
*   **Achtung! (Attention!)**: A warning box stating that the car jack is only for short-term lifting during wheel changes. It emphasizes that the ground must be firm and level, a support base should be used on loose ground, and jack stands must be used if working under the vehicle.

### **Procedural Text**
The document outlines steps for preparation:
1.  **Step 1**: Press the parking brake pedal firmly. Do not release it while the vehicle is raised.
2.  **Step 2**: Shift manual transmissions into 1st or reverse gear; set automatic transmissions to position "P".

### **Technical Illustrations**
There are two black-and-white technical illustrations:

*   **Left Illustration (labeled P40-001-11A)**:
    *   **Components**: Shows a front wheel with a multi-spoke alloy rim. A **Radschlüssel** (lug wrench) is attached to one of the **Radschrauben** (wheel bolts).
    *   **Indicators**: A large red arrow points downward, showing the direction to turn the wrench to loosen the bolts.
    *   **Safety Gear**: Two **Keilen** (wheel chocks) are shown placed in front of and behind the tire.
    *   **Related Text (Step 3)**: Instructs to secure the vehicle against rolling. On level ground, chock the diagonally opposite wheel. On slopes, chock both wheels of the other axle on the downhill side.

*   **Right Illustration (labeled Z222)**:
    *   **Components**: Shows the lower side sill of the car. A tool (the handle of the lug wrench) is being used to pry open a small rectangular **Abdeckung** (cover).
    *   **Function**: This reveals the **Wagenheber-Einsteckrohr** (jack insertion tube).
    *   **Related Text (Steps 4 & 5)**: 
        *   **Step 4**: Unfold the lug wrench and loosen bolts without removing them completely. For the theft-deterrent bolt **(3)**, use the adapter **(4)** (referencing page 111).
        *   **Step 5**: Remove the cover for the jack tube. These tubes are located behind the front wheel arches and in front of the rear wheel arches.

### **Summary of Visible Text and Identifiers**
*   **Page Number**: 112 (bottom left corner).
*   **Image Codes**: "P40-001-11A" and "Z222".
*   **Component References**:
    *   **(3)**: Diebstahlsicherung (Theft-protection bolt/lock)
    *   **(4)**: Zwischenstück (Adapter/Intermediate piece)
*   **Key German Terms**: 
    *   *Wagenheber*: Car jack
    *   *Unterstellböcke*: Jack stands
    *   *Feststellbremse*: Parking brake
    *   *Radläufen*: Wheel arches

[Image: r129_betriebsanleitung_1991_1993_de_p115_img1.jpeg]
This technical document page from a Mercedes-Benz service manual (likely an owner's handbook) provides illustrated instructions for changing a wheel on a vehicle, specifically an R129 model. The page is numbered **113** and is part of a section titled **"Praktische Ratschläge"** (Practical tips).

### Diagram Descriptions

**1. Left Image (Reference 2229):**
*   **Description:** Shows the vehicle being raised using the factory jack.
*   **Components:** Front-left section of the car body, wheel with multi-spoke alloy rim, and a side-mounting jack (**Wagenheber**) inserted into the dedicated jacking point on the side sill.
*   **Connections:** The jack's insert bolt is shown fully inserted into the vehicle's insertion tube.

**2. Middle Image (Reference P40-0002-B13):**
*   **Description:** Shows the front wheel assembly with the wheel removed and a centering pin installed.
*   **Components:**
    *   **Brake Assembly:** Brake disc (rotor) and brake caliper.
    *   **Suspension:** Coil spring and shock absorber strut.
    *   **Wheel Hub:** Features five threaded holes for wheel bolts.
    *   **Component 1:** A **Zentrierbolzen** (centering bolt/pin) is shown screwed into the topmost hole of the wheel hub to support the wheel during mounting/unmounting.

**3. Right Image (Reference P40-0003-B13):**
*   **Description:** Shows the process of remounting the wheel.
*   **Components:** The wheel being aligned with the hub.
*   **Details:** Two red arrows indicate the wheel being pushed onto the hub. The centering pin (from the previous step) is visible protruding through the top hole of the wheel rim to align the bolt holes.

---

### Instructional Text (Translated from German)

**Step 6:** Push the jack's insert bolt completely into the insertion tube. The jack must always stand vertically — even on slopes.
**Step 7:** Raise the vehicle until the wheel has lifted off the ground.
**Step 8:** Unscrew wheel bolts completely. Do not place wheel bolts in sand or dirt. When unscrewing the last wheel bolt, ensure the wheel does not tilt to avoid paint damage.
**Step 9:** Remove the wheel.
**Step 10:** Screw the centering bolt (**1**) from the on-board tool kit into the top threaded hole.
**Step 11:** Slide on the wheel and press it on. Screw in the wheel bolts and tighten slightly. (For wheel bolt details, see the illustration on page 111). For wheel bolts with anti-theft protection, insert the intermediate piece. When screwing in the first wheel bolt, ensure the wheel does not tilt to avoid paint damage. Finally, unscrew the centering bolt and screw in the last wheel bolt.

### Summary of Labels and Numbers
*   **Component 1:** Zentrierbolzen (Centering bolt).
*   **Document References:** 2229, P40-0002-B13, P40-0003-B13.
*   **Page Number:** 113.
*   **Section Title:** Praktische Ratschläge.

[Image: r129_betriebsanleitung_1991_1993_de_p116_img1.jpeg]
This is a technical page from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service or owner's manual, specifically page 114, detailing the process for changing a wheel and checking tire pressure.

### **Technical Diagrams**
The page contains two numbered diagrams:

1.  **Left Diagram (Ref: P40-0026-61A):**
    *   **Description:** Shows a lug wrench (Radschlüssel) applied to a wheel bolt on a car.
    *   **Visual Indicators:** A thick red arrow points clockwise, indicating the direction for tightening the wheel bolts.
    *   **Components:** Car wheel, wheel arch/fender, jack socket point (with wrench inserted), and the wheel wrench itself.

2.  **Right Diagram (Ref: P40-0028-61A):**
    *   **Description:** A schematic of a five-bolt wheel pattern illustrating the correct tightening sequence to ensure even seating.
    *   **Sequence:** The bolts are numbered 1 through 5 in a star pattern:
        *   **1:** Top center
        *   **2:** Bottom right
        *   **3:** Middle left
        *   **4:** Middle right
        *   **5:** Bottom left
    *   **Components:** The diagram features a stylized wheel rim with the Mercedes-Benz star logo in the center hub.

---

### **Technical Specifications & Measurements**
*   **Tightening Torque:** 110 Nm.
*   **Maintenance Interval:** New wheels must have their bolts retightened after **100 to 500 km**.
*   **Tire Pressure Temperature Correction:** Tire pressure changes by approximately **0.1 bar for every 10 °C** change in air temperature.
*   **Pressure Adjustment Example:** If setting pressure in a room at **+20 °C** for use in an outside temperature of **0 °C**, the pressure should be set to the prescribed value **+ 0.2 bar**.

---

### **Visible Text (Translated from German)**

**Main Headings and Sections:**
*   **Reifen-Luftdruck (Tire Air Pressure):** Located in red on the top right.
*   **Hinweise (Notes):** Found in two locations, providing additional instructions.
*   **Beispiel (Example):** Provides a calculation for temperature-adjusted tire pressure.

**Instructional Steps (Left Side):**
*   **12.** Lower the vehicle. Remove the jack and insert the cover for the jack socket pipe.
*   **13.** Fold up the wheel wrench. Tighten all wheel bolts evenly. See the figure for the tightening sequence (star pattern). Tightening torque is **110 Nm**.

*   **Page Number:** 116
*   **Language:** German
*   **Subject:** Headlight maintenance (Adjustment and Bulb Replacement)

---

### **Left Section: Scheinwerfer-Einstellung (Headlight Adjustment)**
This section features an illustration (reference code **P54-0804-8220**) showing the rear view of the headlight assembly with the cover installed.

**Numbered Components:**
1.  **Scheinwerfer-Seitenverstellung:** Headlight horizontal (side-to-side) adjustment screw.
2.  **Scheinwerfer-Höhenverstellung:** Headlight vertical (height) adjustment screw.
3.  **Verschlußbügel für Scheinwerferabdeckung:** Locking wire clip for the headlight cover.
4.  **Scheinwerferabdeckung:** Rear plastic headlight cover.

**Instructions:**
*   Check adjustments regularly.
*   Before adjusting, run the engine.
*   Turn the headlight range control (LWR) to the "0" position.

---

### **Right Section: Glühlampen erneuern (Replace Light Bulbs)**
This section features an illustration (reference code **P54-0805-8220**) showing the rear view of the headlight assembly with the central cover removed, exposing the internal wiring and bulb sockets.

**Bulb Specifications (Numbered Components):**
*   **5. Fern- und Abblendlicht:** High and low beam bulb. Type: **H4**, Specification: **60/55 W**.
*   **6. Stand- und Parklicht:** Standing and parking light bulb. Type: **W 5 W**.
*   **7. Blinklicht:** Turn signal/indicator light bulb. Type: **P 21 W**.

**Wiring and Connections:**
*   A wiring harness is visible entering the main housing and connecting to the sockets for bulbs 5 and 6.
*   Visible wire colors in the diagram include brown (ground), and others that appear to be white and grey with various tracer stripes (standard for MB headlight harnesses).
*   The turn signal bulb (7) is located in a separate outer housing compartment.

**Safety Instructions:**
*   Only touch new light bulbs with tissue paper or similar material (to avoid skin oils).
*   Use only 12-volt bulbs with the correct specified wattage.

This technical page is from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service manual (page 117), detailing the replacement procedures for front and rear light bulbs.

### **Heckleuchten (Rear Lights) Component Diagram**
The center of the page features two diagrams labeled with a reference code **P54-0096-B1**, showing the rear light assembly and its internal bulb carrier.

*   **Upper Diagram:** Shows the exterior lens of the rear light cluster, divided into four numbered sections from left to right.
*   **Lower Diagram:** Shows the internal **Lampenträger** (bulb carrier) with four corresponding bulb positions.

**Bulb Specifications (per the text list):**
1.  **Bremslicht** (Brake light): P 21 W
2.  **Rückfahrlicht** (Reverse light): P 21 W
3.  **Fahrerseite** (Driver’s side): **Schlußlicht/Parklicht/Nebelschlußlicht** (Tail/Parking/Rear fog light) - P 21/4 W
    **Beifahrerseite** (Passenger’s side): **Schlußlicht/Parklicht** (Tail/Parking light) - P 21/4 W
4.  **Blinklicht** (Turn signal): P 21 W

### **Rear Bulb Replacement Procedure**
A third diagram at the top right (**P54-0096-B13**) illustrates how to access the bulbs from inside the trunk.
*   **Verriegelungstaste (1):** A locking button indicated by a straight red arrow. To release the bulb carrier, this button is pushed inward.
*   **Lampenträger:** A curved red arrow indicates the carrier then swings outward/downward to reveal the bulbs.
*   **Instruction:** Bulbs are removed by pressing down, turning to the left, and pulling out.

### **Front Light Bulbs (Text Only)**
The left column provides instructions for lights in the engine compartment. No diagram is provided for these, but specific components are named:
*   **Fern- und Abblendlicht** (High and low beam): Mentions a **Verschlußbügel (3)** (locking bail) and **Abdeckung (4)** (cover).
*   **Stand- und Parklicht** (Standing and parking light): Uses the same bail and cover, with a removable **Lampenhalter** (bulb holder).
*   **Blinklicht** (Turn signal): Mentions a **Lampenhalter** that is turned to the left and removed.

### **Visible Text and Metadata**
*   **Heading:** "Glühlampenwechsel vom Motorraum aus durchführen." (Perform bulb change from the engine compartment.)
*   **Warning:** "Achtung! Glühlampen und Lampenträger können sehr heiß sein." (Warning! Bulbs and bulb carriers can be very hot.)
*   **Sidebar:** "Praktische Ratschläge" (Practical Tips) in a vertical red banner.
*   **Page Number:** 117.
*   **Internal Codes:** P54-0096-B1 and P54-0096-B13.

This image is page 118 from a technical service document for a Mercedes-Benz R129, detailing the location and maintenance of license plate lights and electrical fuses.

### **Image 1 (Left): Kennzeichenleuchten (License Plate Lights)**
*   **Component:** License plate light assembly located at the rear of the vehicle.
*   **Measurement/Spec:** The text specifies a "Soffitte 5 W" (5W festoon bulb).
*   **Callouts:**
    *   **1:** Points to the two mounting screws on either side of the light lens.
*   **Text (Translated):** "License plate lights (5W festoon). Unscrew both mounting screws (1) and remove the light."

### **Image 2 (Center): Elektrische Sicherungen (Electrical Fuses - Engine Compartment)**
*   **Components:**
    *   **1 (Hauptsicherungskasten):** Main fuse box, a large rectangular box with a latching lid.
    *   **2 (Zusatzsicherungsdose):** Auxiliary fuse box, a smaller unit located behind the main box, near the brake booster.
*   **Identifier:** A small code "2708" is visible in the bottom right corner of this specific photograph.
*   **Text (Translated):** "Electrical fuses. In the engine compartment: 1 Main fuse box, 2 Auxiliary fuse box."

### **Image 3 (Right): Elektrische Sicherungen (Electrical Fuses - Trunk)**
*   **Component:**
    *   **3 (Zusatzsicherungsdose):** Auxiliary fuse box located in the trunk (Kofferraum) against the rear wall.
*   **Identifier:** Image reference "P54-0003-31 3A" is located in the bottom right.
*   **Text (Translated):** "In the trunk on the rear wall: 3 Auxiliary fuse box."

### **General Text Instructions (Right Column):**
*   **Safety Warning:** Fuses must not be patched or bypassed.
*   **Closure:** After replacing a fuse, ensure the fuse box cover is closed properly.
*   **Diagrams:** The fuse assignment/layout is located on the inside of the covers for the main and auxiliary fuse boxes. A diagram of the fuse arrangement is also located in the lid of the main fuse box.
*   **Maintenance:** Identify the cause of a short circuit before replacing a blown fuse. Spare fuses are located in the main fuse box. Pay attention to the correct amperage and color-coding.

**Page Number:** 118 (Bottom left)

[Image: r129_betriebsanleitung_1991_1993_de_p123_img1.jpeg]
This image is a technical instruction page from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service document detailing the "Starthilfe" (jump-starting) procedure. It is page 121 from the "Praktische Ratschläge" (Practical Advice) section.

### **Component Names & Locations**
*   **Batterie (Battery):** Located in the trunk behind the right side paneling (*"im Kofferraum hinter der rechten Seitenverkleidung"*).
*   **Starthilfekabel (Jump leads / Booster cables):** Required for the procedure.
*   **Lenkschloß (Steering lock):** Where the key is turned to position 0.
*   **Katalysatoranlage (Catalytic converter system):** Mentioned in the context of cooling down before repeated start attempts.
*   **Pluspole & Minuspole (Positive & Negative terminals):** Connection points on the batteries.
*   **Polklemmen (Terminal clamps):** Must be insulated.

### **Measurements & Technical Specifications**
*   **Voltage:** 12 Volt (battery from the donor vehicle).
*   **Cable Cross-section:** Minimum 25 mm² (*"mindestens 25 mm² Leitungsquerschnitt"*).
*   **Temperature:** Mentioned that a discharged battery can freeze at approximately -10 °C and must be thawed before jump-starting.

### **Connection Sequence**
1.  **Connect:** First the positive terminals (+), then the negative terminals (-).
2.  **Disconnect:** First the negative terminals (-), then the positive terminals (+).

### **Visible Text (Transcription)**

**Main Header:**
*   **Starthilfe** (Jump-starting)

**Instructional Text:**
*   "Ist die Batterie entladen, kann der Motor mit Starthilfekabeln (mindestens 25 mm² Leitungsquerschnitt) und der Batterie (12 Volt) eines anderen Fahrzeuges gestartet werden."
*   "Die Batterie befindet sich im Kofferraum hinter der rechten Seitenverkleidung."
*   "Schlüssel im Lenkschloß in Stellung 0 drehen."
*   "Motor des anderen Fahrzeuges mit höherer Drehzahl laufen lassen."
*   "Zuerst die Pluspole und dann die Minuspole der Batterien mit den Starthilfekabeln verbinden."
*   "Motor wie üblich starten."
*   "Wenn der Motor läuft, zuerst das Starthilfekabel von den Minuspole und dann von den Pluspolen lösen."

**Safety Warning (Achtung!):**
*   "Während der Starthilfe nicht über die Batterien beugen - Verätzungsgefahr!" (Danger of acid burns - do not lean over batteries).
*   "Nicht mit offener Flamme in der Nähe der Batterie hantieren, nicht rauchen, Funkenbildung vermeiden - Explosionsgefahr." (Explosion hazard - no open flames, smoking, or sparks).

**Notes (Hinweise):**
*   "Die Starthilfe kann bei kaltem Motor und abgekühlter Katalysatoranlage durchgeführt werden. Mehrere sowie lang andauernde Startversuche sind jedoch zu vermeiden."
*   "Eine entladene Batterie kann bei ca. -10 °C gefrieren. Sie muß vor der Starthilfe unbedingt aufgetaut sein."
*   "Nur Starthilfekabel mit isolierten Polklemmen benutzen!"

**Sidebar & Footer:**
*   **Praktische Ratschläge** (Practical Advice - vertical text on right)
*   **121** (Page number)

This technical page from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service manual (page 122) provides instructions for towing the vehicle.

### Image Details
*   **Image ID:** P31-0001-013 (located at the bottom right of the photograph).
*   **Visual Content:** A black and white photograph showing the front bumper area. A rectangular access flap is shown in a partially removed position, hanging by two retention straps. Behind the flap, a heavy-duty metal **towing eye (hook)** is visible. A red curved arrow indicates the direction to pull the flap from its recess.

### Component Names and Locations
*   **Front Towing Eye (vordere Abschleppöse):** Located on the right side of the vehicle, behind a removable flap in the bumper.
*   **Rear Towing Eye (hintere Abschleppöse):** Located on the right side under the rear bumper.
*   **Flap (Klappe):** A rectangular cover in the bumper providing access to the front towing eye.
*   **Bumper (Stoßfänger):** The exterior body panel where the flap and towing eyes are situated.

### Operational Instructions
*   **Removing the Flap:** Reach into the recess of the flap and pull it away from the bumper.
*   **Reinstalling the Flap:** Hook the bottom part of the flap in first, then press firmly at the top to secure it.
*   **Towing Method:** The document recommends using a **tow bar (Abschleppstange)**. However, the preferred method is transport via a **specialized transporter or trailer**.

### Technical Notes and Safety Warnings
*   **Power Assistance:** When the engine is not running, power assistance for the **service brake (Betriebsbremse)** and **power steering (Servo-Lenkung)** is unavailable. This requires significantly higher physical force to brake and steer the vehicle.
*   **Lighting and Indicators:** If the **hazard warning lights (Warnblinkanlage)** are on while towing, operating the **combination switch (Kombi-Schalter)** will cause only the selected side (left or right) to flash. Returning the switch to its center position restores full hazard flashing.
*   **Regulatory Compliance:** Users are advised to observe specific national towing regulations.

### Text Summary (Translated/Transcribed)
*   **Title (Red):** An- und Abschleppen des Fahrzeuges (Towing the vehicle)
*   **Heading (Bold):** Abschleppen (Towing)
*   **Heading:** Hinweise: (Notes:)
*   **Page Number:** 122 (bottom left corner)

This image is a page of technical maintenance instructions from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service document or owner's manual, specifically page 126. It provides detailed care instructions and recommended products for various vehicle components.

### **Components and Maintenance Instructions**

**1. Kombi-Instrument (Instrument Cluster)**
*   **Recommended Agents:** MB Autoshampoo, neutral dish soap, or mild detergent.
*   **Instructions:** Wipe with a lint-free cloth dampened in a lukewarm solution. Abrasive cleaners should not be used.

**2. Lackierung, lackierte Anbauteile (Paintwork, painted add-on parts)**
*   **Recommended Products:** MB Glanzkonservierung (Gloss Preserver), MB Polish, MB Lackreiniger (Paint Cleaner), MB Polierwatte (Polishing Cotton).
*   **Application Rules:** Do not apply in direct sunlight or on a warm hood.
*   **Usage Details:**
    *   **MB Glanzkonservierung:** Protects paint and maintains gloss.
    *   **MB Polish:** Used for heavier soiling and removing minor scratches from painted wood trim.
    *   **MB Lackreiniger:** For cleaning older or weathered paint.
    *   **MB Lackstift (Touch-up Pen) & MB Sprühdose (Spray Can):** For quick, provisional repair of small paint chips/damage.
    *   **MB Polierpaste (Polishing Paste):** For heavily soiled or weathered paint and polishing out small scratches.
*   **Note (Hinweis):** To avoid staining, keep these products away from non-painted add-on parts such as door handles and rubber seals.

**3. Zierteile (Trim parts)**
*   **Recommended Product:** MB Chrompflege (Chrome Care) for ongoing maintenance.

**4. Leichtmetallräder (Alloy Wheels)**
*   **Recommended Products:** MB Autoshampoo, MB Pflegemittel (Care Product), and MB Reiniger für Leichtmetallräder (Alloy Wheel Cleaner).
*   **Instructions:** Should ideally be cleaned weekly. Use a soft sponge, plenty of lukewarm water, and MB Autoshampoo.
*   **Heavier Soiling:** Use MB Pflegemittel for normal dirt and MB Reiniger for heavy dirt. Always follow the specific instructions for use.

### **Visible Text Summary**
*   **Headings:** Kombi-Instrument, Lackierung, lackierte Anbauteile, Zierteile, Leichtmetallräder.
*   **Key Terms:** MB Autoshampoo, MB Polish, MB Glanzkonservierung, MB Lackreiniger, MB Polierwatte, MB Lackstift, MB Sprühdose, MB Polierpaste, MB Chrompflege, MB Pflegemittel.
*   **Page Number:** 126 (located at the bottom left).

This technical document is page 128 from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service manual, detailing the operation, battery replacement, and synchronization of the infrared remote control key fob.

### Illustrations and Components

The page features three black-and-white technical illustrations with red numbered callouts and directional arrows:

*   **Left Illustration (Remote Operation):** Shows the infrared remote control unit.
    *   **1**: Transmit button (the Mercedes-Benz star).
    *   **2**: Transmitter output window and battery control indicator light. Lines radiate from this point to symbolize the infrared signal.
    *   **Technical Label:** "2203" located at the bottom right of the illustration.
*   **Middle Illustration (Battery Compartment):** Shows two views of the remote for battery access.
    *   **3**: Sliding release latch on the side of the unit, marked with a red arrow indicating the direction to push.
    *   **4**: Battery cover, shown being slid away from the main body with a red arrow.
    *   Inside the compartment, four coin-cell batteries are visible.
    *   **Technical Label:** "P80-0003-B13" located at the bottom right.
*   **Right Illustration (Receiver):** Shows the exterior car door handle.
    *   **5**: Infrared receiver window located on the end of the door handle assembly.
    *   **Technical Label:** "P72-5001-B13A" located at the bottom right.

### Text Content (German)

The document contains three main instructional sections in German:

**1. Infrarot-Fernbedienung prüfen (Checking infrared remote control)**
*   **Batterien kontrollieren (Checking batteries):** Instructions state that if the transmit button (1) is pressed for longer than one second, a light should briefly appear at the transmitter output (2) to indicate the batteries are functional. If it does not light up, the batteries must be replaced.

**2. Batterien wechseln (Changing batteries)**
*   Instructions explain moving the release (3) sideways to pull off the battery cover (4).
*   It advises ensuring the correct installation position (polarity) of the new batteries.
*   The cover (4) should be slid back on until it clicks into place.
*   **Hinweis (Note):** Dispose of depleted batteries in an environmentally friendly manner.

**3. Anlage synchronisieren (Synchronizing the system)**
*   Explains that synchronization is necessary if the transmitter has been without power (batteries removed) for several minutes.
*   **Procedure:** Point the transmitter (2) at a receiver (5) and press the transmit button (1) briefly. Then, within approximately 30 seconds, manually lock or unlock the vehicle at a door or trunk lock using the mechanical key. The remote will then be ready for use.

### Additional Details
*   **Page Number:** "128" is printed at the bottom left corner.
*   **Color Palette:** The document is primarily grayscale with red used for instructional arrows and component numbers.

*   **Main Title:** Roadster-Verdeck mechanisch verriegeln (Manually locking the roadster soft top)

Then, set the soft top compartment cover (**2**) in a vertical position.

This is a technical service document page from a Mercedes-Benz R129 manual, detailing the manual operation of the soft top.

### **Components and Labels**
*   **(4) Stoffhaltebügel:** Fabric retaining bow (rear portion of the soft top).
*   **(5) Verdeckrahmen:** Convertible top frame (front portion of the soft top).
*   **(6) Kappen:** Caps/covers located on the windshield header near the sun visor pivots.
*   **Innensechskantschlüssel:** Allen wrench (hex key) used for manual locking.

### **Instructional Steps and Actions**
The page describes steps 6 through 8 of a procedure:

*   **Step 6:** Place the fabric retaining bow **(4)** in a vertical position and rest the convertible top frame **(5)** on the windshield frame.
*   **Step 7:** Swing the sun visors to the side to expose and remove the caps **(6)** on both the left and right sides.
*   **Step 8:** Lock the convertible top frame **(5)** on both the left and right sides. This is done by inserting an Allen key and turning it in three specific stages toward the center of the vehicle:
    1. Left side: Turn until the first notch/detent.
    2. Right side: Turn until the second notch/detent.
    3. Left side: Turn until the second notch/detent.

### **Visible Text**
*   **Bottom Left Page Number:** 130
*   **Image IDs:**
    *   Left image: `P77-0003-B13A`
    *   Middle image: `P77-0011-B13A`

    *   **6.** Stoffhaltebügel (4) senkrecht stellen und Verdeckrahmen (5) auf den Rahmen der Windschutzscheibe legen.
    *   **7.** Sonnenblenden zur Seite schwenken. Kappen (6) links und rechts abnehmen.
    *   **8.** Verdeckrahmen (5) links und rechts verriegeln – Innensechskantschlüssel in 3 Stufen zur Fahrzeugmitte drehen:

        3. Links bis zur zweiten Raste

This image is a technical page (page 131) from a German-language Mercedes-Benz R129 service or owner's manual detailing the manual operation procedure for the convertible soft top. It consists of three illustrations and instructional text sections 9 through 12.

### Component Overview
*   **(1) Gabelschlüssel:** Open-end wrench (special tool).
*   **(2) Verdeckkastendeckel:** Soft top compartment lid (rear deck lid).
*   **(4) Stoffhaltebügel:** Soft top fabric bow (rear portion of the convertible top).
*   **(7) Arrow:** Indicates pushing the wrench forward.
*   **(8) Abdeckungen:** Covers inside the trunk.
*   **(9) Arrow:** Indicates pressing down on the wrench.
*   **Überrollbügel:** Roll bar.
*   **Bolzen:** Bolt/Pin for locking mechanism.
*   **Verschlußzapfen:** Locking pins/lugs.
*   **Rotmarkierter Hebel:** Red-marked lever in the trunk area.

### Illustration and Instruction Details

#### Left Illustration (Ref: P77-0009-B13 B)
*   **Action:** Shows the vehicle exterior with the soft top compartment lid (2) closed. An open-end wrench is inserted behind the roll bar.
*   **Text (Section 9 & 10):**
    *   **9.** Close the soft top compartment lid (2). Lock the left and right latches; insert the open-end wrench between the roll bar and the compartment lid onto the bolt and push forward as indicated by arrow (7).
    *   **10.** Fold the fabric top bow (4) down and insert the locking pins into the latches.

#### Middle Illustration (Ref: P77-0012-B13A)
*   **Action:** Close-up of the trunk interior side wall.
*   **Text (Section 11):** Slide the covers (8) upwards and remove them (found on both the left and right sides in the trunk).

#### Right Illustration (Ref: P77-0810-B13)
*   **Action:** Shows the open-end wrench applied to a lever mechanism in the trunk. Red arrows indicate pushing down on the fabric top bow (4) and pushing down on the wrench (9).
*   **Text (Section 12):** 
    *   Place the open-end wrench onto the red-marked lever.
    *   Press down on the fabric top bow (4) and lock it in 3 sequential steps using the wrench:
        1. Left side until the first notch.
        2. Right side until the second notch.
        3. Left side until the second notch.
    *   Only press the wrench down (9) until the lock is heard to engage.
    *   Advice: Have the soft top checked at a Mercedes-Benz Service Station.

### Additional Metadata
*   **Vertical text in right margin:** "Praktische Ratschläge" (Practical Advice).
*   **Page number (bottom right):** 131.
*   **Wire colors/specific measurements:** No wiring or specific numerical measurements are present, aside from the 3-step locking sequence.

[Image: r129_betriebsanleitung_1991_1993_de_p134_img1.jpeg]
This image is a technical page (page 132) from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service or owner's manual detailing the manual procedure for locking the hardtop (Coupé) roof.

### **General Information**
*   **Title:** Coupé-Dach mechanisch verriegeln (Mechanically locking the coupé roof)
*   **Context:** Instructions for manually locking the roof if the automatic system fails. It specifies using a combined open-ended/Allen wrench from the vehicle's onboard toolkit.

### **Component and Diagram Details**

#### **Image 1 (Top Left): Trunk Preparation**
*   **Component 1:** Sliding plastic covers located on the left and right sides of the rear compartment (trunk) trim, near the roof mechanism hinges.
*   **Action:** The diagram shows an arrow indicating that these covers should be slid upwards and removed.
*   **Reference Code:** P65-3012-B13A (partially visible).

#### **Image 2 (Top Middle): Rear Locking Mechanism**
*   **Component 2:** The rear portion of the hardtop roof.
*   **Component 3:** A special open-ended wrench (Gabelschlüssel) from the toolkit.
*   **Mechanical Part:** A red-marked lever within the mechanism behind the removed cover (1).
*   **Action:**
    *   **Arrow 2** indicates pressing down on the roof.
    *   **Arrow 3** indicates the downward motion of the wrench when attached to the red lever to engage the locking notches.
*   **Reference Code:** P65-3001-B13A.

#### **Image 3 (Top Right): Interior Preparation**
*   **Component 4:** Small circular plastic caps/covers located on the upper interior windshield frame, near the sun visor mounting points.
*   **Action:** The sun visor is shown pivoted to the side to reveal the cap (4), which must be removed to access the front locking points.
*   **Reference Code:** P65-3011-B13A.

### **Transcribed Text and Instructions**

**Introductory Text:**
> *Bei einem Defekt der Automatik kann das Dach auch mechanisch verriegelt werden. Für diese Arbeit liegt dem Bordwerkzeug ein kombinierter Gabel- bzw. Innensechskantschlüssel bei.*
> (In the event of a defect in the automatic system, the roof can also be locked mechanically. For this work, a combined open-ended or hexagon socket wrench is included with the vehicle tools.)

**Step 1:**
> *1. Im Kofferraum links und rechts die Abdeckungen (1) nach oben schieben und abnehmen.*
> (1. In the trunk on the left and right, slide the covers (1) upwards and remove them.)

**Step 2:**
> *2. Gabelschlüssel auf den rotmarkierten Hebel aufstecken. Dach niederdrücken (2) und mit dem Gabelschlüssel in 3 Stufen verriegeln:*
>   *1. Links bis zur ersten Raste*
>   *2. Rechts bis zur zweiten Raste*
>   *3. Links bis zur zweiten Raste*
> *Den Gabelschlüssel nur soweit niederdrücken (3), bis die Verriegelung hörbar einrastet.*
> (2. Attach the open-ended wrench to the red-marked lever. Press down the roof (2) and lock it in 3 stages with the open-ended wrench: 1. Left until the first notch; 2. Right until the second notch; 3. Left until the second notch. Only press down the open-ended wrench (3) until the lock audibly clicks into place.)

**Step 3:**
> *3. Sonnenblenden zur Seite schwenken. Kappen (4) links und rechts abnehmen.*
> (3. Swing the sun visors to the side. Remove caps (4) on the left and right.)

This image is page 133 from a Mercedes-Benz R129 technical manual or owner's handbook, titled "**Praktische Ratschläge**" (Practical Advice). It contains three technical diagrams and instructions for roof locking, rear seat removal, and ashtray removal.

### Section 1: Roof Locking (Left)
*   **Diagram Identifier:** P81-0806-B13A
*   **Components:**
    *   **Windshield frame/header rail:** Shows the interior upper trim where the roof latches.
    *   **Hex wrench (Allen key):** Shown inserted into the manual locking point.
    *   **Red arrow:** Indicates a clockwise rotation (towards the center of the vehicle) for the tool.
*   **Instructions (Summary):** Describes manually locking the roof using a hex key in three steps towards the vehicle center:
    1. Left side until the first notch.
    2. Right side until the second notch.
    3. Left side until the second notch.
    *   It advises having the "Coupé-Dach" (hardtop) checked at a service station.

### Section 2: Rear Seat Removal (Center)
*   **Diagram Identifier:** P92-0052-B13
*   **Components:**
    *   **Rear seat cushions:** Two separate base cushions.
    *   **Component 1:** Release buttons located on the lower front edge of each seat cushion.
*   **Removal Instructions:** Press buttons (1), lift the front of the seat cushion, and pull forward.
*   **Installation Instructions:** Slide the rear edge of the cushion under the backrest until it stops, then press down the front until it clicks into place.

### Section 3: Ashtray Removal (Right)
*   **Diagram Identifier:** P81-0004-R13
*   **Components:**
    *   **Center console:** Top-down view.
    *   **Component 1:** Sliding release button located next to the lighter.
    *   **Component 2:** Removable ashtray insert.
*   **Removal Instructions:** Open the roll-top cover (Jalousie), push sliding button (1) to the left, which causes the insert (2) to pop up slightly for removal.
*   **Installation Instructions:** Place the insert back and press down until it clicks into place.

### Additional Text and Markings
*   **Right Margin:** A vertical red bar contains the text "**Praktische Ratschläge**".
*   **Bottom Right:** Page number "**133**".
*   **Language:** All text is in German.

This is a page from a technical service document for a Mercedes-Benz R129, specifically page **134**. The page provides instructions for replacing the windshield and headlight wiper blades.

### Section 1: Windshield Wiper Blades (Windschutzscheibe)

**Technical Diagram (Top Left):**
*   **Image type:** Close-up black-and-white photograph of a windshield wiper blade assembly.
*   **Components and Labels:**
    *   **Red Arrow 1:** Points to the locking button (*Sicherungstaste*) on the wiper blade.
    *   **Red Arrow 2:** Indicates the downward sliding direction to remove the blade from the arm.
    *   **White Box with Number 3:** Indicates the retaining lugs or "noses" (*Nasen*) at the end of the wiper arm where the blade is inserted.
    *   **Reference Number:** "1351" is printed in the bottom right of the image frame.

**Instructional Text (German):**
*   **Wischerblätter erneuern:** "Aus Sicherheitsgründen vor dem Erneuern des Wischerblattes den Lenkschloßschlüssel abziehen." (For safety reasons, remove the steering lock key before replacing the wiper blade.)
*   **Ausbauen (Removal):** Fold the wiper arm forward. Press down the locking button (**1**), slide the wiper blade down (**2**) and remove it.
*   **Einbauen (Installation):** Press down the locking button on the new wiper blade. Insert the wiper blade between the noses (**3**) on the wiper arm and guide it into the end of the wiper arm. Then push the locking button up until it clicks into place.
*   **Hinweise (Notes):**
    *   Do not open the hood when the wiper arm is folded forward.
    *   Instead of the entire wiper blade, just the wiper rubber can be replaced. It is recommended to have this done at a Mercedes-Benz service station.

---

**Technical Diagram (Top Right):**
*   **Image type:** Black-and-white line drawing showing the movement of a headlight wiper blade relative to the arm.
*   **Components and Labels:**
    *   **Red Arrow 1:** Shows the pivoting motion required to disengage the blade from the arm.
    *   **Red Arrow 2:** Shows the position of a new blade being placed perpendicular to the arm for installation.
    *   **Red Arrow 3:** Shows the pivoting motion to snap the new blade into its locked position.
    *   **Reference Number:** "P82-0011-51S" is printed in the bottom right of the image frame.

**Instructional Text (German):**

*   **Einbauen (Installation):** Position the wiper blade transversely (perpendicular) to the wiper arm (**2**) and pivot it (**3**) until it clicks into place.

This is a technical page from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service manual (page 135) titled "Praktische Ratschläge" (Practical Advice). It contains instructions for manually opening the fuel flap and detailed serpentine belt routing diagrams for different engine models.

### 1. Manual Fuel Flap Release (Left Image)
This section describes how to manually open the fuel filler flap if the central locking system fails.
*   **Component 1:** A round manual release knob located in the trunk on the right side behind the side paneling.
*   **Action:** An arrow indicates that the knob should be pulled back (towards the rear of the car) to release the fuel flap.
*   **German Text:** "Tankklappe mechanisch öffnen. Läßt sich die Tankklappe durch eine Störung nicht öffnen, den Entriegelungsknopf zurückziehen und Tankklappe öffnen. Der Entriegelungsknopf befindet sich im Kofferraum rechts hinter der Abdeckung."

### 2. Serpentine Belt Routing Diagrams (Middle and Right Images)
These diagrams show the routing of the serpentine belt (Keilrippenriemen) around various engine pulleys. The belt should be installed following the numerical order of the pulleys, starting at the tensioner pulley (1).

#### Keilrippenriemen (Serpentine Belt) Legend:
1.  **Spannrolle mit Spannvorrichtung:** Belt tensioner pulley with tensioning device.
2.  **Kurbelwelle:** Crankshaft pulley.
3.  **Umlenkrolle / Fahrzeuge mit Klimaanlage oder Klimatisierungsautomatik: Kältekompressor:** Deflection pulley; for vehicles with AC, this is the air conditioning compressor.
4.  **Lüfter:** Engine fan pulley.
5.  **Luftpumpe:** Air pump pulley (Smog pump).
6.  **Drehstromgenerator:** Alternator pulley.
7.  **Umlenkrolle:** Deflection/Idler pulley (present only on 300 SL / 300 SL-24).
8.  **Lenkhelfpumpe:** Power steering pump pulley.
9.  **Kühlmittelpumpe:** Coolant/Water pump pulley.

#### Belt Length Measurements (Abmessungen):
*   **300 SL:** 2,330 mm
*   **300 SL with AC or automatic climate control:** 2,415 mm
*   **300 SL-24:** 2,445 mm
*   **500 SL:** 2,523 mm

#### Specific Routing Notes:
*   **300 SL, 300 SL-24 (Middle Diagram):** Features 9 pulleys. The alternator (6) is at the bottom left, the air pump (5) is above it, and an idler pulley (7) is above that.
*   **500 SL (Right Diagram):** Features 8 pulleys. The air pump (5) is at the bottom left, and the alternator (6) is positioned above it. There is no pulley #7.

This technical document page (number 138) from a German-language Mercedes-Benz R129 service manual or owner's guide details the locations of vehicle identification plates and explains the use of vehicle data cards.

### **Section: Typschilder (Identification Plates)**

This section provides instructions on providing identification numbers when ordering original parts. A central line-drawing illustration of an R129 SL-Class with an open hood uses numbered red arrows to indicate the location of specific information:

*   **1. Typschild (Identification Plate):** Located on the front radiator cross member, visible when the hood is open.
*   **2. Fahrzeug-Ident.-Nr. (Vehicle Identification Number - VIN):** Located on the firewall/bulkhead on the passenger side (for left-hand drive vehicles).
*   **3. Karosserie-Nr., Lack-Nr. (Body Number, Paint Code):** Located on a plate attached to the upper radiator support beam.
*   **4. Motor-Nr. (Engine Number):** The text specifies that for the **500 SL**, this is located at the **hinten links** (rear left) of the engine block.

### **Section: Fahrzeug-Datenkarten (Vehicle Data Cards)**

This section explains that the data cards contain all essential technical specifications for the vehicle. It includes a simplified diagram of a data card (labeled with a red "1") showing a grid for various codes.

*   **Datenkarte Nr. 1 (Data Card No. 1):** The text states this card is sent to the owner. Because it contains the **Schlüssel-Nr. (Key Number)**, the document strongly advises against keeping it inside the vehicle. This number is required to order replacement keys from a Mercedes-Benz service station.
*   **Datenkarte Nr. 2 (Data Card No. 2):** This card does not include the key number and is stored within the vehicle's **Wartungsheft (Service Booklet)**. Presenting it at a service workshop helps facilitate administrative processing.

### **Visible Text and Notations**

*   **Main Header (Left):** "Typschilder" (Red)
*   **Instructional Text (Left):** "Bei der Bestellung von Originalteilen bitte Fahrzeug-Identifizierungs- und Motor-Nr. angeben." (When ordering original parts, please provide vehicle identification and engine numbers.)
*   **Main Header (Right):** "Fahrzeug-Datenkarten" (Red)
*   **Body Text (Right):** Explains the distribution and security precautions for Data Cards No. 1 and No. 2.
*   **Page Number:** "138" (Bottom left)
*   **Illustration Reference Numbers:**
    *   Under the car: "P00-0001-52/4X"
    *   Under the data card diagram: "9073"

This image is a technical information page from a Mercedes-Benz R129 service manual (page 145), written in German. It provides specifications and maintenance instructions for engine coolant and brake fluid.

### **Section 1: Korrosions-/Frostschutzmittel (Coolant/Anti-corrosion/Anti-freeze)**

The text on the left explains that coolant concentration should be checked before winter or annually in hot climates. This check is part of every Mercedes-Benz service. It emphasizes using only approved coolant to avoid system damage.

**Coolant Capacity Table (Füllmenge - Korrosions-/Frostschutzmittel):**
The table lists fill quantities in liters (l) required to achieve specific levels of frost protection for different engine types.

| Vehicle Model (Typ) | Frost Protection to -37 °C | Frost Protection to -45 °C |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **300 SL** | 5.75 l | 6.30 l |
| **300 SL-24** | 5.75 l | 6.30 l |
| **500 SL** | 7.50 l | 8.25 l |

---

### **Section 2: Bremsflüssigkeit (Brake Fluid)**

The text on the right (headed in red) explains that brake fluid absorbs moisture over time, which lowers its boiling point. This can lead to vapor bubbles and reduced braking effectiveness under high stress (e.g., mountain driving).

**Maintenance Instructions:**
*   **Replacement Interval:** Brake fluid should be renewed every 2 years, preferably in the spring.
*   **Specification:** Use only Mercedes-Benz approved brake fluid.

---

### **Layout and Marginalia**
*   **Vertical text (right margin):** "Betriebsstoffe" (Operating Fluids/Supplies) printed in red.
*   **Page Number (bottom right):** 145.
*   The document contains no part numbers, wire colors, or schematic connections as it is a data and informational text page rather than a diagram.

[Image: r129_betriebsanleitung_1991_1993_de_p148_img1.jpeg]
This image is a technical page from a German-language Mercedes-Benz R129 service document (page 146) detailing fuel requirements and ignition timing adjustment.

### **Technical Illustration**
The illustration shows a circular **EZL-KAT adjustment plug (Abgleichstecker)**.

*   **Component Name:** EZL-KAT Adjustment Plug.
*   **Face Markings:**
    *   Large white text: **"EZL-KAT"**.
    *   Central icon: Mercedes-Benz three-pointed star logo.
    *   Peripheral numbers: **1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7** arranged around the dial.
    *   Alpha markings in red: **"S"** at the top center and **"N"** at the 3 o'clock position.
*   **Housing/Connection:** The circular dial is mounted on a rectangular connector base which has a wiring harness exiting from the bottom right.
*   **Current Setting:** An arrow on the housing points to the **"S"** position.

---

### **Text Content**

#### **Kraftstoffe (Fuels)**
This section describes fuel requirements:
*   Engines are designed for **premium unleaded fuel** (Superkraftstoff) for optimal performance and economy.
*   **Premium Unleaded:** Minimum 95 ROZ (RON) / 85 MOZ (MON).
*   **Temporary Use:** Unleaded regular fuel, minimum 91 ROZ / 82.5 MOZ.
*   **Note for 300 SL-24 and 500 SL:** Using regular unleaded increases engine temperature. Avoid prolonged full-throttle driving.

#### **Zündeinstellung anpassen (Adjusting Ignition Timing)**
This section explains how to adjust the ignition timing based on fuel quality.
*   **300 SL-24, 500 SL:** Ignition timing is adjusted automatically by the engine's anti-knock control system.
*   **300 SL:** Ignition must be manually adjusted using the **Abgleichstecker (Adjustment Plug)**.
*   **Standard Setting:** The plug must normally be set to position **"S"**.
*   **Exceptional Use:** If regular unleaded fuel is used, the plug must be set to position **"N"** to prevent engine damage.
*   **Location:** The plug is located in the engine compartment (reference to page 152).

#### **Einstellen (Setting Instructions)**
Steps to adjust the plug:
1.  **"Stecker bis zum Anschlag herausziehen"**: Pull the plug out until it stops.
2.  **"Stecker in die gewünschte Stellung drehen"**: Turn the plug to the desired position (observe the marking on the housing):
    *   **S:** Operation with premium unleaded fuel (Superkraftstoff).
    *   **N:** Operation with regular unleaded fuel (Normalkraftstoff).
3.  **"Stecker wieder eindrücken"**: Push the plug back in.

**Page Number:** 146 (Visible in bottom left corner).

This image is an informational page from a Mercedes-Benz service document, likely for the R129 chassis, titled **"Was Sie an der Tankstelle wissen müssen"** (What you need to know at the gas station). It provides technical specifications for fluids, capacities, and bulb types.

### **Text and Specifications by Section:**

#### **1. Kraftstoff (Fuel)**
*   **Type:** Unleaded premium fuels (Bleifreie Superkraftstoffe), minimum **95 ROZ/85 MOZ**.
*   **Reference:** Further information can be found on page 146.
*   **Capacity:** Tank capacity is approximately **80 l**, with a reserve of approximately **10 l**.
*   **Instruction:** Fill the fuel tank only until the pump nozzle shuts off; do not overfill.

#### **2. Motorenöl (Engine Oil)**
*   **Reference:** Oil level check procedure is on page 106.
*   **Measurement:** The difference in quantity between the lower and upper marks on the dipstick is approximately **2 l**.
*   **Reference:** Approved engine oils are listed on page 142.

#### **3. Reifen-Luftdruck (Tire Pressure)**
*   **Reference:** Prescribed tire pressures are listed in a table located on the fuel filler flap.
*   **Note:** Different tire pressures apply to CTS tires compared to standard tires.

#### **4. Scheibenwaschanlage / Scheinwerfer-Reinigungsanlage (Windshield Washer / Headlight Cleaning System)**
*   **Capacity:** Reservoir capacity is approximately **5 l**.
*   **Additives:** Mix **50 ml** of **MB Konzentrat „S”** into the reservoir.
*   **Antifreeze Mixture:** For freezing conditions, use **1.25 l** of **MB Konzentrat „W”** and **25 ml** of **MB Konzentrat „S”**.

#### **5. Glühlampen (Light Bulbs)**
The document lists the following bulb types and wattages:
*   **High and Low Beam (Fern- und Abblendlicht):** H 4 (60/55 W)
*   **Fog Light (Nebelscheinwerfer):** H 1 (55 W)
*   **Standing/Parking Light (Standlicht/Parklicht):** W 5 W
*   **Turn Signal (Blinklicht):** P 21 W
*   **Brake Light (Bremslicht):** P 21 W
*   **Tail/Parking Light (Schlußlicht/Parklicht):** P 21/4 W
*   **Tail/Parking/Rear Fog Light (Schluß-/Park-/Nebelschlußlicht):** P 21/4 W
*   **License Plate Light (Kennzeichenbeleuchtung):** 5 W (Soffitte/Festoon bulb)
*   **Reversing Light (Rückfahrlicht):** P 21 W

This is a scanned page from "THE STAR" magazine (July-August 2010 edition, page 57) titled "TECHNICAL CHECKPOINTS." It provides advice for potential buyers or owners of the Mercedes-Benz R129 SL-Class.

### **Text Content Summary**

The document lists seven specific checkpoints for evaluating an R129:

1.  **Potential mechanical issues:** Focuses on wiring harness failures in 1993–1995 models (repair costs estimated at several thousand dollars, parts roughly **$500–$700**). It mentions checking head gaskets on **M104 engine** 300SLs, 5th gear overdrive issues on **5-speed automatics** in 500 and 600 models, and mechanical odometer failure on early models. It also notes the complexity of the **Acceleration Slip Regulation (ASR)** system.
2.  **Wind-protection screen:** Standard starting in 1993, also called a **"draught-stop."** It is stored in a compartment in the trunk held by three straps.
3.  **Removable hardtop:** Notes that late-model SLs have larger seals at the A-pillars and windshield, making hardtops not universally interchangeable.
4.  **Panoramic hardtop roof:** Identifiable by its black exterior and rounder shape. Estimated market value is **$500 to $2500**. Compatibility is stated for model years **1995 and later**.
5.  **Soft top and rollover bar:** Recommends checking for hydraulic leaks at the A-pillars and pistons. Notes that original soft tops have a **checkered pattern** inside and that the canvas is a two-piece design.
6.  **Special editions:** Lists rare versions including the **Mille Miglia Edition**, **Designo Edition**, **40th Anniversary Roadster Edition (1997)**, **Special Edition (1998)**, **Final Edition (2000)**, **SL Edition (2000)**, and **Silver Arrow Edition (2002)**. It also mentions rare **5-speed manual** 300SLs from 1990–1991.
7.  **AMG models:** Advises checking for builder-signed engine badges and serial numbers. Lists production counts:
    *   **SL55:** 65 units
    *   **SL60:** 633 units
    *   **SL70:** 150 units
    *   **SL73:** 42 units
    *   Total R129 production: **204,940 units**.

### **Image Description**

The bottom of the page features a high-contrast photograph showing the rear three-quarter view of a dark-colored Mercedes-Benz R129 SL.

*   **Visible Components:**
    *   **Hardtop:** Installed on the vehicle, featuring a large wrap-around rear glass window.
    *   **Trunk Lid:** Features the centered Mercedes-Benz three-pointed star emblem.
    *   **Taillight:** The left rear assembly is visible, featuring the characteristic horizontal ribbing.
    *   **Wheels:** The rear left wheel is visible, showing a 5-spoke alloy design.
    *   **Bodywork:** Includes the rear bumper and left rear quarter panel.

### **Measurements and Values Mentioned**
*   **Production numbers:** 65 (SL55), 633 (SL60), 150 (SL70), 42 (SL73), 204,940 (Total R129).
*   **Monetary values:** $500–$700 (harness parts), $500–$2500 (panoramic roof).
*   **Years:** 1990, 1991, 1993, 1995, 1997, 1998, 2000, 2002, 2010 (document date).

## **Unlocking** 

Turn the key to the left to the stop and remove in the vertical position. 

## **Locking** 

Turn the key to the right to the 60° position and remove in the vertical position. 

## **Notes** 

On vehicles with infrared remote control the central locking element for the trunk lid is no longer connected electrically as of 01/94. For this reason the central locking can no longer be controlled with the mechanical key from the trunk lid.

Turn the key to the right as far as the stop and remove in the horizontal position. The trunk lid now remains locked when the doors are unlocked by the central locking. 

## **Anti-theft protection** 

If the vehicle is locked from the outside, the trunk lid and the tank flap can only be opened after being unlocked from the outside. Only the respective door can be opened via the interior control lever or the handle on the door panel. 

## **Emergency unlocking of the tank flap** 

In the event of the central locking not functioning, the tank flap can be unlocked manually via a red emergency unlocking knob on the element for the tank flap.

## **Example of basic function sequence for unlocking vehicle via the driver's door.** 

By turning the key to the left in the lock cylinder the electric switch in the actuator is switched over via a rod. This switch then supplies a positive voltage to the supply pump via its control line. 

The supply pump starts up and produces pressure, which is led to all pneumatic elements via a system of lines. The diaphragms in the elements are pressed upwards, operating the locks via a rod and unlocks them. 

The tank flap element unlocks the flap directly. At the same time the electrical switches of the actuators in the passenger door and the trunk lid are actuated likewise by the pneumatic part of the element and supply positive voltage to the supply pump in the same 

© 2007 Mercedes-Benz USA, LLC

Page 6 of 21 

Repair information 

way as the mechanically operated switch in the actuator of the driver's door. 

If the system reaches a pressure significantly greater than 450 mbar, the supply pump is switched off by the pressure switch. If the pneumatic line system and the elements are now vented again via the supply pump, the system is depressurized and the unlocking procedure is completed. 

The locking procedure is carried out similar to the unlocking procedure. However if the supply pump is energized with a negative control voltage, the direction of rotation of the pump motor is reversed and thus the vacuum required for locking is produced. 

**==> picture [22 x 14] intentionally omitted <==**

## **Version 2 as of 12/94, as of 09/95** 

## **Example of basic function sequence for unlocking vehicle with infrared remote central locking (IRCL)** 

Point transmitter window on remote control at receiver and press remote control button. The infrared control module then supplies positive voltage to the supply pump via a control lead. 

The supply pump starts up producing pressure which flows through a system of lines to all pneumatic elements. The diaphragms in the elements are pressed up actuating the locks via a linkage and unlocking the vehicle. 

The tank flap element unlocks the flap directly. 

When a pressure of approx. 450 mbar is reached in the system, a pressure switch switches off the supply pump. 

This relieves the pressure in the pneumatic system of lines and elements via the supply pump - the system is no longer under pressure and the unlocking operation is completed. 

The locking operation is accomplished in a similar manner to the unlocking operation. However, negative control voltage is fed to the supply pump the next time the remote control button is pressed. 

The direction of rotation of the pump motor is reversed so that the pump provides the vacuum required for locking.

This image is a technical function schematic for a Mercedes-Benz R129 central locking system, specifically labeled as "Version 1 up to 11/94" with regional indicators for the USA and Japan (J).

### **Components and Functional Blocks**
The diagram depicts the following major components and their sub-elements:
*   **Key**: The starting point of the operation.
*   **Lock Cylinder**: Receives mechanical input from the key.
*   **Left Door Actuator**: Contains an **electrical switch** and a **pneumatic element**.
*   **Right Door Actuator**: Contains an **electrical switch** and a **pneumatic element**.
*   **Trunk Lid Lock Actuator**: Contains an **electrical switch** and a **pneumatic element**.
*   **Supply Pump for Central Locking**: The central control unit, containing **electronic control** logic and a **pneumatic pump** that produces pressure.
*   **Locks**: Separate mechanical lock mechanisms for the left door, right door, and trunk lid.
*   **Tank Flap Element** and **Tank Flap**: The locking mechanism for the fuel filler door.

### **Operational Flow and Connections**
The diagram uses three types of lines to indicate different functions:
*   **Single thin line**: Mechanical function
*   **Double thin line**: Electrical function
*   **Triple thin line**: Pneumatic function

#### **Initial Triggering Action**
1.  The **key** is turned with an **anti-clockwise rotation** into the **lock cylinder** (mechanical).
2.  The lock cylinder **unlocks** the local mechanical **lock** (mechanical).
3.  Simultaneously, the lock cylinder **operates** the **electrical switch** within the left door actuator (mechanical).

#### **System Logic and Power Distribution**
1.  The **electrical switch** in the left door actuator (or alternatively from the right door or trunk lid actuators) **informs** the **electronic control** unit within the central supply pump (electrical).
2.  The **electronic control** unit then **controls** the internal **pneumatic pump** to produce pressure.
3.  The pneumatic pump **operates** the **pneumatic elements** in all actuators simultaneously via pneumatic lines:
    *   **Left door actuator**
    *   **Right door actuator**
    *   **Trunk lid lock actuator**
    *   **Tank flap element**

#### **Final Mechanical Output**
1.  Once pressurized, each **pneumatic element** (left door, right door, and trunk lid) physically **unlocks** its respective mechanical **lock** (mechanical).
2.  The **tank flap element** physically **unlocks** the **tank flap** (mechanical).

Repair information

## **Pressurizing and depressurizing (vehicles up to approx. 12/93)** 

In order to make possible locking immediately after unlocking or vice versa, without increased energy expenditure, the pneumatic lines to the doors are pressurized or depressurized with two electrical switchover valves. 

The two valves hold the lines open in rest position. When the supply pump starts up, these valves are earthed and lock the lines. As soon as the supply pump switches off after locking or unlocking, the earth control to the valves is cancelled. The valves open and pressurize or depressurize the pneumatic lines. 

## **Pressurizing and depressurizing (vehicles as of approx. 01/94)** 

The two pressurizing and depressurizing valves below the driver's and front passenger's seat are no longer used as of the introduction of the bi-pressure pumps with immobilization output. 

For the pressurizing and depressurizing function of the central locking, the supply pump runs briefly in the opposite direction after reaching the shut-off pressure. The pressure in the system is thus reduced. As a result the vehicle can be locked immediately after unlocking or vice versa without increased use of energy. 

## **Emergency opening** 

In order to facilitate the release of occupants of a vehicle which has been locked from the inside, in the event of a severe accident, the vehicle unlocks automatically. 

Unlocking takes place when an acceleration of more than 4g or a vehicle inclination of more than 26° occurs and the ignition key is in position "1 or 2". 

To do this, the control unit for the roll-over bar controls the supply pump for the central locking, which initiates unlocking of the vehicle after a 5 second delay. 

## **D.   Components** 

## **1.   Supply pump (M14/1, M14/2)** 

There are 7 versions of supply pumps: 

a)   Supply pump for the central locking and vacuum M14/1 (production up to 09/91). 

Supply pump with 2 pneumatic connections. Identification **ZV** : vacuum and pressure for central locking 

Identification **PU** : vacuum for auxiliary consumers for supporting the intake manifold vacuum 

b)   Supply pump for the central locking with orthopaedic seat backrest, vacuum and 

interior central locking (special equipment up to 12/93). 

Supply pump with 4 pneumatic connections. Identification **ZV** : vacuum and pressure for central locking Identification **PU** : vacuum for auxiliary consumers for supporting the intake 

manifold vacuum 

Identification **IZV** : vacuum and pressure for interior central locking

## **Note** 

Since the pin assignment in the electrical connector has been changed, supply pumps with/without output for control of the starter lockout relay (production breakpoint 01/94) and supply pumps with input for CL interior control switch (production breakpoint 09/95) are not interchangeable. 

## **Technical data** 

|Maximum current consumption|A|7.5|
|---|---|---|
|Closed-circuit consumption - terminal 30|mA|≤1|
|Closed-circuit consumption - terminal 15 (auxiliary consumers)|mA|≤100|
|Pressure switch off point for central locking and interior central locking|mbar|≥450|
|Switching time|about s|1|
|Safety switching time in the event of leaks in the central locking or interior central locking|about s|20  30|
|Safety switching time in the event of leaks in the auxiliary consumers|about s|70|



## **The control unit for the central locking** 

The supply pump is supplied with a negative control voltage for locking and a positive control voltage for unlocking from the actuators. 

The supply pump produces pressure for unlocking and vacuum for locking (about 600 mbar). 

The change of the pressure direction is controlled by the clockwise or anticlcokwise running of the motor and the pump. It is thus ensured, that the command which was last issued is carried out. 

In the event of serious leaks, the supply pump switches off after 25 - 30 seconds (safety switching time). The electronic control has several logic functions, which avoid faulty switching and disturbances. In addition the control unit has a leakage current detection, whereby the leakage current cannot result in automatic functions, since the control inputs concerned are switched off.

text:
Repair information 

Page 14 of 21 

The interior central locking is unlocked, when: 

- positive voltage is supplied to the control input of the interior central locking. 

- a positive voltage is applied to the control input of the driver's door or passenger door and when simultaneously the control unit of the comfort/ATA is earthed briefly. 

- positive voltage is applied to the control input of the trunk lid. 

- positive voltage is applied to the control input of the infrared remote control. 

The interior central locking is connected to the central locking by a 3/2 directional control valve on the supply pump. Actuation of the control input of the interior central locking will only ever operate the interior central locking. If the interior central locking is operated indirectly by the central locking, then the central locking is always operated first.In the event of severe leakage in the system the pump switches off after a continuous running time of 20 - 30 seconds. 

## **Control unit for infrared remote control** 

If the supply pump receives a positive signal via the control input of the infrared remote operation, it carries out an unlocking process. Likewise, the interior central locking unlocks, if neces¬sary, provided that the control input of the interior central locking is earthed. 

When there is a negative signal to the control input of the infrared remote control the central locking locks, and if need be, the interior central locking. 

## **Control unit for the orthopedic driver's seat backrest** 

The M14/2 supply pump produces the necessary pressure for the orthopedic driver's seat backrest. 

It applies pressure to the storage reservoir up to a maximum of 590 mbar. 

If this pressure reduces to about 200 - 230 mbar the supply pump starts up again until the maximum pressure of 590 mbar has been reached again. 

In the event of severe leakage in the pressure system (orthopedic driver's seat backrest) the pump switches off after a continuous running period of 60 - 70 seconds. 

If the supply pump constantly switches on and off in time intervals shorter than 17 ± 2 seconds due to slight leaks, these switching operations are added up by a leakage detection system and the pump switches off after 31 switching operations. This process is interrupted by switching off the ignition, and starts all over again. The added-up switching operations are erased, as soon as the supply pump has not been switched on for longer than 17 ± 2 seconds. 

**PU** identification (special equipment) Connection for orthopaedic driver's seat backrest.

## **2. Actuators (S47, S48, S49)** A combined actuator is installed in the driver's and passenger door and in the trunk lid. This actuator has an electrical and a pneumatic connection for a quick-fit connection. The electrical and pneumatic function of all actuators is the same. The electrical switch in the upper part of the actuator is permanently connected to the positive terminal and to ground. The two-way switch provides the supply pump with a positive control voltage for unlocking and a negative control voltage for locking. The lower chamber of the actuator is applied with pressure for unlocking and with vacuum for locking. The electrical and pneumatic part of the actuator can be separated by a sliding sleeve with a catch, so that the lock can also be operated, when the actuator is still applied with pressure or vacuum. Adjustment of the sliding sleeve (a) is prevented by an integrated support (arrow) on the actuator S47 and S48. When the connecting rod is loaded against the lock the adjusting lock is made inoperative. In this way the actuator is in the installation position. Adjustment errors on the door actuators are excluded. The central locking with multipoint operation is a single line system, in which the pneumatic elements are operated through pressure or vacuum (dual pressure central locking). 

It is possible to carry out central locking or unlocking from the outside from both drivers' doors and from the trunk lid by operating the key or the infrared remote control. The central locking can be operated inside via an interior control lever. All doors, the trunk lid and the tank flap are included in the central locking. 

## **Notes** 

On vehicles with infrared remote control as of 01/94 the central locking cannot be locked and unlocked centrally from the trunk lid lock with the mechanical key. Control of the interior central locking with the mechanical key is only possible from the lock cylinder in the glove box lock. 

On vehicles as of 09/95 the central locking can be operated from inside with the CL interior control switch. 

On and vehicles as of 09/95 the central locking can be operated from outside with the infrared remote control or with the mechanical key from the lock cylinder in the driver's door or the lock in the trunk lid. From the inside the central locking can be operated with the CL interior control switch. 

## **B.   Operation** 

## **Driver's door** 

The central locking can always be operated when the driver's door is closed. From outside with a key, (turning to the right to the stop for locking, turning to the left to the stop for unlocking). 

## **Note** 

As of introduction of the stage 2 drive authorization system (12/94), approx. 09/95 the central locking can be operated from outside only with the infrared control. Operation with the mechanical key remains possible for the models. 

Vehicles up to 08/95 

The central locking can be operated from inside with the interior control lever.

## **Unlocking** 

Turn the key to the left to the stop and remove in the vertical position. 

## **Locking** 

Turn the key to the right to the 60° position and remove in the vertical position. 

## **Notes** 

On vehicles with infrared remote control the central locking element for the trunk lid is no longer connected electrically as of 01/94. For this reason the central locking can no longer be controlled with the mechanical key from the trunk lid.

Turn the key to the right as far as the stop and remove in the horizontal position. The trunk lid now remains locked when the doors are unlocked by the central locking. 

## **Anti-theft protection** 

If the vehicle is locked from the outside, the trunk lid and the tank flap can only be opened after being unlocked from the outside. Only the respective door can be opened via the interior control lever or the handle on the door panel. 

## **Emergency unlocking of the tank flap**
